skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Run a two-axis review of changes since a fixed point. It compares the diff against repository standards and the originating issue, PRD, or spec.
skill.summary: Review branch changes against coding standards and product requirements.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.user_title: Review Changes Against Standards and Specs
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss whether a change follows project standards and whether it implements the requested work. This skill separates both checks and reports findings side by side.
actual_capabilities: Compares HEAD against a user supplied commit, branch, tag, or merge base.
Checks changed code against repository standards and a Fowler code smell baseline.
Checks changed code against an issue, PRD, spec file, or user supplied requirements.
Runs standards and spec reviews in separate subagents to keep findings distinct.
Aggregates the two reports under Standards and Spec headings.
limitations: Requires a valid Git fixed point and a non-empty diff.
Cannot verify a spec when no issue, PRD, or requirement source is available.
Depends on available repository documentation for project-specific standards.
Produces review findings, not automatic fixes or test execution results.

use_cases.title: Review a feature branch before opening a pull request
use_cases.description: Compare the branch with main and find standards violations or missed requirements before reviewers see it.

use_cases.title: Audit work against an issue or PRD
use_cases.description: Check whether the implementation matches the requested scope and identify behavior that was not requested.

use_cases.title: Separate style concerns from product correctness
use_cases.description: Receive independent reports for coding standards and spec alignment so one axis does not hide the other.

prompt_templates.title: Review since main
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review using the default integration branch as the fixed point.

prompt_templates.title: Review since a commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since commit abc123 and use docs/product/checkout-prd.md as the spec source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with an explicit fixed point and requirement document.

prompt_templates.title: Review a work in progress branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changes since origin/main. Use linked issue references from the commits when available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate pull request preparation with issue lookup.

prompt_templates.title: Review against strict standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Review since release-2026. Focus on documented standards, the smell baseline, and any implementation gaps from the matching PRD.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release review with standards and spec coverage.

output_examples.output: A Standards section lists convention or smell findings from the diff. A Spec section lists missing requirements, scope creep, or incorrect behavior.

output_examples.input: Review since abc123 using the checkout PRD.
output_examples.output: The response separates code quality concerns from PRD alignment and ends with counts and worst findings for each axis.

output_examples.input: Review since origin/main, but there is no spec.
output_examples.output: The Standards review still runs, while the Spec section states that no spec was available.

best_practices: Provide the exact fixed point for the diff before starting the review.
Point to the issue, PRD, or spec when commit messages do not identify it.
Keep repository standards documents current so the standards axis has clear evidence.
anti_patterns: Asking for a review without a fixed point when multiple baselines are possible.
Treating smell baseline findings as hard failures without project context.
Merging Standards and Spec findings into one ranked list.

faq.question: What fixed points can I use?
faq.answer: You can use a commit SHA, branch name, tag, merge base, or a relative ref such as HEAD~5.

faq.question: Does this skill make code changes?
faq.answer: No. It reviews the diff and reports findings. It does not apply fixes.

faq.question: What happens if there is no spec?
faq.answer: The Spec review is skipped and the final report states that no spec was available.

faq.question: How are standards chosen?
faq.answer: The skill looks for repository standards files and also applies a baseline set of code smell heuristics.

faq.question: Why are two subagents used?
faq.answer: Separate subagents keep standards findings and spec findings independent so one review axis does not dominate the other.

faq.question: Can this review pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the branch base or target branch as the fixed point for the pull request diff.
